sections.text: Introduction

This document outlines the testing 
procedure P1, which must be performed according to this table and 
may be subject to be changed according to directives of 
Central Chemical Laboratories.

The technical material is taken from operation 
protocol for El Zone, in addition to the experience of Central Chemical 
Laboratories at Egyptian Company for Electricity Transmission; Egyptian 
Electricity Holding Company.

This test method covers the 
determination of particle size distribution of catalyst and catalyst carrier 
particles using an electroconductive sensing method and is one of several 
valuable methods for measurement of particle size.

The range of particle 
sizes investigated was 20 to 150 m equivalent spherical diameter. The technique 
is capable of measuring particles above and below this range. The 
instrument used for this method is an electric current path of small dimensions 
that is modulated by individual pulses of amplitude proportional to the particle 
volume.
Summary of Test Method

A carefully 
 dispersed, dilute suspension of the sample in a beaker filled with an 
 electrolyte is placed in the counting position on the instrument sample 
 stand. The suspension is forced through a restricting aperture. Each passing 
 particle is recorded on an electronic counter, and the data are 
 accumulated according to selected particle size intervals for subsequent 
 processing.

The instrument response is 
 proportional to liquid displacement by the particle volume. Equivalent 
 spherical diameter is commonly used to express the particle size.
Safety Precautions

items:
The sample must be taken as MPIS 
 document no. TD-SS-003-r2

Make sure the sample bottle is correctly 
 labeled

Make sure the sample bottle is free from 
 dust and dirt.

The sample must be kept away from 
 exposure to direct sunlight.

As oil sample must be free from water it 
 has to be taken under dry and clear environmental conditions.

sections.text: Environmental Recommendations

items:
The test must be done in a suction 
 chamber.

Using solvents such as benzene and other 
 for cleaning the valve parts is dangerous, it will expose lunge to very 
 hazardous and carcinogenic chemicals, you have to wear your berating mask.

Don't throw the sump oil in the sewage 
 because this oil will prevent the sewage treatment process collect it in tight 
 containers and return it back to the vendor to recycle it. Always remember 
 that "this oil is load for your wastes but it's valuable material for them".
Avoid oil spillage to the ground.

Procedure Follow 
instrument manufacturer's instruction manual for instrument settings. (The CCL 
Uses EL Zone 280 PC instrument ).

items:
Turn on the EL Zone 280
 PC instrument (Observe pump working and side lamp on)

Turn on the 
 printer and observe lights on front panel.
Turn on the monitor and then the computer.

The following sub menu will be presented:
 Command prompt
 Editor
 Msdos Q Basic
 EL zone 280 PC
 M.S. windows real mode
 M.S. windows std mode
 Place the cursor bar at the EL Zone line and press the enter button on the
 keyboard to activate. Wait
 and the computer will display the El Zone program.

Check that the screen displays 
 (A) the sparkle screen (B) the analyse
 screen and (C) the count
 box.

Wash the EL zone glassware by the following procedure:
 (A) With the orifice tube in place, put beaker of clean electrolyte on
 sample stand
 and beaker of clean electrolyte at side of fill tubing.
 (B) Move the EL zone control valve to the flush position and place the fill
 tube
 into the beaker of clean electrolyte.
 (C) When the system is full, remove the fill tube so that the system
 empties.
 (D) Repeat one or two times and leave the system full and control valve at
 the
 count position.
Prepare 100 ML of blank electrolyte and place on the sample platform.

Check through the microscope to see that the orifice is clear. If not, use
 the black back-pressure
 plunger with the control valve in the count position and a gentle push to
 clear or remove tube and follow the instructions in the EL Zone manual.

If the orifice is clear, Then move or leave the control valve in the
 vacuum position and go over
 to the computer screen. Using the mouse, place the pointer on analyse and
 press the left hand
 button on the mouse to pull down the sub-menu. Place the pointer on
 normalize and press the
 left hand button once more. Wait for the normalize procedure to complete.
 Return the control
 valve to the count position.

Place the pointer on the file and press mouse button and then select
 new. At the resulting
 sub-menu of histogram/lots/counts, just press on ok.

Answer the questions regarding sample and operator 
ID before pressing ok..
Move the control valve to vacuum.
Check that the orifice is clear.
Wait for the mercury to go below the start contact.

Put the pointer at the 
analyze command and select start.

Return the control valve to 
count and wait when the mercury goes past the stop contact, the
 count will be displayed in the count box along with the VOL TIME REF
 like so.
 # reading 1
 # reading 2
 # reading 3 
We take average of them
 # reading 4 
 # reading 5
 # reading 6

Place the pointer at 
File and press. Select Save as, histogram ok, and enter
 the name Blank press
 Save. At replace existing file say yes.

Put the pointer at 
new in the counts box and press and then select All counts. Fill in sample 
ID
 info

Place pointer at 
display and select erase data.
Prepare oil sample and place on platform.

Move control valve to vacuum and wait for the mercury to go below the 
start
 contact.

Press analyze and then 
start before moving the control valve to count
 position. Repeat until all
 6 counts are displayed E.G.
 # reading 1
 # reading 2
 # reading 3 
We take average of them
 # reading 4 
 # reading 5
 # reading 6

Select Acceptable counts by placing the pointer in the relevant box and
 pressing mouse. An (X)
 should appear next to accepted counts

Place pointer at 
Average and press to obtain average count. Take note of
 number for next step.

Place the pointer at 
Set-up and select Status enter average count into the
 Total box on the left
 hand column. Press ok.

Place pointer at 
Convert and select Total this will normalize the histogram
 content to the
 average count.

Place pointer at 
Options and select String Execute choose macro Final and
 say open. Wait press finish when completed

Select Options and 
percentiles. Place pointer at Load and press ok.
Place pointer at FILE and select print say ok.

To repeat the process, place the pointer at 
new in the counts
box and select All counts then proceed as before.
Presentation of Data

The
 instrument measures the volume of each particle. Assuming 
 all the particles in the sample have the same denisty, relative volume and 
 weight can be considered to be interchangeable; therefore, cumulative and 
 differential volume or weight percent can be printed or graphed directly 
 from the accumulated data.

Results for samples containing mixed densities should be 
 expressed as volume percent instead of weight percent and cannot be compared 
 to a
 direct weight analysis method.
Calculation

Count of Particle Size/100 
ml oil = Reading of Instrument X 100
Precision

It's based on the results of a multilaboratory 
 study and using the procedures and definitions of practice E 177 and 
 practice E691 the single-laboratory, single day repeatability is 2.3 % (2S 
 %) of the mean of the measurements of the volume percent media 
 equivalent spherical diameter. The 
 multilaboratory, multiday reproducibility is 4.6 % (2S %) of the 
 mean of the measurements of the volume percent media equivalent 
 spherical diameter, when a common calibration standard is used.
Recommended Test and Interpretation
Particle Counting

Care 
 shall be taken to ensure that no foreign material is introduced during 
 sampling.

It 
 shall be emphasized that there is a need for the proper cleaning and 
 flushing of new oil systems and operating systems after maintenance on the 
 oil systems. In certain cases the use of extra oil filtration equipment on a 
 temporary basis could be an advantage. If the concentration of particles 
 increases suddenly , investigate immediately to determine the source and 
 check the functioning of the purification equipment. In the case of 
 corrosion products also check the rusting characteristics of the oil. Note 
 that high counts can also be caused by gas bubbles and foam suppressants so 
 that a visual examination using a microscope is often desirable. Particle 
 analysis can also be very useful to determine the source of the 
 contamination.
Interpretation of Test Data and Recommended Action

rows:
Source of Particulates may be: 
 Make up oil.
 Dust or ash 
 entering system
 Wear condition 
 in system.

Review limits with 
 equipment manufacturer and if required identify particles. Locate 
 and eliminate source. Clean system oil by filtration and/or 
 centrifuging.
